rationale: Identity verification was done correctly using name + zip. However, multiple policy violations occurred: (1) The agent performed an order-changing write (exchange_delivered_order_items) without first restating the exact change and obtaining explicit confirmation to proceed; the user’s selection of a replacement item is not the same as confirming the specific exchange action, costs, and terms. (2) The agent cited specific item IDs (original item 2757705742 and new item 4063058357) and a refund amount ($15.63) that are not supported by the tool outputs—this appears fabricated. The retrieved order #W3470184 explicitly shows one earbuds item with IPX4, not IPX7; the claimed IPX7 item ID is not evidenced. (3) The agent used the “delivered order” exchange tool without confirming the order’s status/eligibility. (4) The final confirmation claimed the exchange was processed and a refund issued without tool evidence reflecting success or the refund amount. These issues violate the requirements to not invent details, to confirm before writes, and to provide correct final information.
